Dirty Bomb is not completely shit F2PFPS. It does not have pay to win elements.

Aah, ok, this makes sense. What's the weapon stuff like in the paying part? Just cosmetics? Or something else?

It does have some "pay to win" elements to be honest. You can unlock anything with gameplay, but paying money does allow you to unlock items much more quickly. Those items most definitely affect gameplay as well, in that you do not have the ability to play some classes until you've accumulated the in-game credits to unlock the class. Thus far, they've been rotating the classes week to week that are playable without an unlock, though if you previously unlocked one of the selections, you do not get a different class available to play.

Also, there are "loadout cases" that you can earn through gameplay and purchase with in-game credits. These cases will change weapons and perks for a class and can massively effect the viability and effectiveness of some classes. Paying money likewise allows you to purchase more of those cases, but they are all RNG in what you receive with each. That in itself is both infuriating and fair, but if the game is going to be taken seriously as a "competitive" multiplayer game, they are going to need to remove the RNG and the unlock elements to actually make it worthwhile. Or allow one to just purchase the game to play with all items available. They've been pushing the serious competition in it, and something has to give.

Dirty Bomb is a lot of fun, and I've been playing it a lot recently with my friends.

If you remember Brink, it's basically Brink. The combat is squad-based and objective-based in relatively small maps, and works well with the 6 on 6 size. The gunplay is a bit rudimentary for my taste, but it's not bad. Positioning isn't as important as in Counter-Strike. It's pretty close to TF2 in terms of the way the game plays out.

There are a a few annoying mechanics (chucking healthpacks/ammopacks), but it has a lot of charm. As others have noted, the recent Phantom class addition will need to be nerfed a bit. The competitive gameplay could ultimately be pretty strong, and it's definitely not pay to win in any dimension.
